title: Polynomial-time split solver existence
statement: For every pair of natural numbers $C,e$, there exist a finite Turing machine over the Boolean alphabet and a natural number $c$ such that, on every Boolean word $w$, the machine halts within $c(|w|+1)^{e+2}$ steps and outputs the pairing of the prefix of $w$ of length $i$ with the remaining suffix when $i$ is the least number satisfying $i+C(i+1)^e=|w|$; if there is no such $i$, it outputs the empty word.
replaced:
For all constants $C$ and $e$ there exist a machine $M$ and a constant $c$
computing, within $c\,(n+1)^{e+2}$ steps on inputs of length $n$, the
function sending $w$ to the pair encoding of the split of $w$ at the least
$i$ with $i + C\,(i+1)^{e} = \abs{w}$, and to the empty word when no such $i$
exists.
